abstract: the ligo-virgo-kagra collaboration has reported the results for searches for sub-solar mass components in compact binary coalescence during observing run o4a. no detection candidates were identified, but the most significant seven triggers were reported. we present the results of bayesian parameter inference on these triggers. five of the triggers show agreement between the bayesian parameter estimation and the search pipeline trigger. our results show that three of the triggers may contain a possible sub-solar mass component. parameter estimation indicates that the other two events, if real, would be neutron star - black hole binaries. the remaining two triggers do not provide informative parameter estimation. we also study three o4a compact binary coalescence triggers, and one o3 trigger, that have been noted by three other groups, and our parameter estimation indicates that three of these may contain a sub-solar mass component. we study the data quality associated with these triggers. finally, we discuss the challenges for parameter estimation on compact binary coalescence events containing a sub-solar mass component: long signal duration, possible small chirp masses, possible small mass ratios, and data quality issues over potentially hundreds of seconds of data.

title: type-ii quasinormal modes of dilaton--euler--heisenberg ads black holes
abstract: in this paper, we investigate type-ii quasinormal modes (qnms) of a magnetically charged dilaton--euler--heisenberg black hole in anti-de sitter (ads) spacetime. the type-ii includes coupled gravitational, dilaton and electromagnetic perturbations. its coupled equations are derived for $\ell=0,1,2$ modes and the qnm frequencies are calculated by employing direct integration and chebyshev pseudospectral methods, giving consistent results. for nondegenerate dipole ($\ell=1$) mode at fixed curvature, the nonlinear correction starts at order $q^2$ for electromagnetic-led branch and at order $q^4$ for scalar-led branch. in this case, stronger ads curvature enhances reduction of the electromagnetic-led real frequency for positive coupling, while gravitational-led quadrupole real frequency changes weakly with charge. as the curvature weakens, the dipole frequencies approach the ads normal-mode scale and their damping decreases. we find that all modes computed have negative imaginary parts for nonextremal black holes, implying this black hole is stable against type-ii perturbations. furthermore, we explore the connection between thermodynamic phase transition and qnms for $\ell=0$ dilaton. for a subcritical isobaric process, the qnm real frequency of $\ell=0$ dilaton decreases with increasing temperature of small black holes, while it increases with increasing temperature of large black holes. at coexistence, the damping rate for large black holes is about 4.28 times that for small black holes.

title: the kerr metric in canonical harmonic coordinates to all orders
abstract: we give in closed form the transformation from boyer--lindquist coordinates to the canonical harmonic coordinates of the kerr metric, to all orders in newton's constant and in the spin. this is the canonical harmonic chart selected by the mpm prescription and by the harmonic-gauge einstein recursion sourced by the kerr multipoles, with the residual homogeneous freedom fixed by the boundary conditions. the chart is the real, time-reversal-covariant combination of the two radial harmonic functions underlying the cook--scheel coordinates, which differ from it by a definite residual harmonic transformation. the proof rests on a classification of the residual harmonic freedom. rotational covariance, parity, time reversal and analyticity in the spin allow a decaying homogeneous solution beyond the linear field only in the spatial components at third post-minkowskian order, with angular degree $\ell=p+2$ at spin order $a^p$. this sector is a pure gauge mode, equivalent to an mpm gauge moment. the exact chart selects the representative in which this third-pm homogeneous mode vanishes; imposing the same condition on the recursion removes the only residual ambiguity and fixes its solution uniquely. as a consequence, the canonical mpm iteration needs no finite-part regularisation and no harmonicity correction at any order. we give the exact gothic metric and the post-minkowskian coefficients in closed form through fifth order, where an arctangent function first appears at fourth order. we find agreement with recent canonical mpm and amplitude-based results at fourth order, and we verify the construction in exact arithmetic through fifth order and twelfth order in the spin, with code made publicly available.

title: test of gravitational redshift by optical clocks at different latitudes
abstract: general relativity predicts that frequency comparisons between clocks are affected by both gravitational and kinematic time dilation. while the kinematic contribution has been tested with high accuracy, experimental tests of the gravitational redshift remain comparatively less stringent. here, we measure the frequency shift between two earth-fixed optical atomic clocks at different potentials and compare it to the redshift predicted by general relativity using independent geodetic measurements. the observed shift agrees with the prediction, testing the gravitational redshift at the $4.6 \times 10^{-5}$ uncertainty level, improving ground-based tests by a factor two. previous ground-based tests separated the clocks mainly vertically. for clocks at different latitudes, their height difference is governed not only by the gravitational potentials at their locations but also by the centrifugal potentials caused by earth's rotation. as both contributions can partially cancel, the gravitational contribution can be considerably larger than their height difference suggests. in this work, a separation of the clocks by $4^\circ$ in latitude enhances their sensitivity to a gravitational redshift violation threefold, to the equivalent of an approximately 1200 m difference in height for small latitudinal separation. our results establish earth's rotation as a so far unexploited resource for advancing ground-based tests of the gravitational redshift towards the sensitivity of previous space-based experiments.

title: coronagraphic time-delay interferometry: fundamental steps towards concrete applications
abstract: the laser interferometer space antenna (lisa) is a future space-based gravitational wave (gw) observatory. central to lisa data analysis is time-delay interferometry (tdi), which reduces otherwise overwhelming laser frequency noise. in previous work, we explored coronagraphic tdi, a sky-dependent null-stream channel which cancels the gw signal of a point-like source when pointed at its sky position. because this property relies only on the geometric response of lisa, coronagraphic tdi is a candidate for model-agnostic sky localization. here, we address three challenges which arise when analyzing realistic lisa data: (i) spacecraft motion; (ii) signal superposition; (iii) instrumental noise. we derive a second-generation coronagraphic tdi variable and its analytic noise model, and show that it reduces laser frequency noise in the presence of spacecraft motion while still recovering the position of the source. using pairs of galactic binaries (gbs), we find that sources can be localized independently provided they do not overlap in frequency, even when they share the same sky position, whereas sources overlapping in frequency can only be localized if one dominates by a factor of ~100 in amplitude. this is confirmed by the analysis of a simulation containing a massive black hole binary and 49 verification gbs. finally, we introduce a statistical test based on the analytic noise model, which provides well-calibrated confidence regions for the sky position of the source. applying it to gbs in the presence of instrumental noise, we find that the geometric response alone only weakly constrains the sky position: even at signal-to-noise ratios of order 10^4, 90% confidence regions span ~10^3 deg^2. these are fundamental steps towards applications of coronagraphic tdi to lisa data, such as sky localization and glitch discrimination, which we discuss.

title: diffusing the assumptions: towards realistic lisa stochastic component separation with physics-aware simulation-based inference
abstract: simultaneous global-fit inference of the numerous sources observed by the laser interferometer space antenna (lisa) depends on accurate modeling of its stochastic components: instrumental noise, the galactic foreground, and astrophysical or stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds (sgwb). realistic features such as non-gaussian transients and data gaps challenge traditional likelihood-based pipelines, creating an opportunity for simulation-based inference (sbi) to augment traditional analyses. here, we present an sbi framework for lisa stochastic component separation built on the simformer, a transformer trained with diffusion or flow matching that ingests the full time-delay interferometry cross-spectral matrix via a physics-aware embedding. we progressively relax standard simplifying assumptions on simulated 11.6-day datasets containing a loud foreground and a faint power-law sgwb. with unequal arms and per-link noise freedom, the networks match 17-dimensional mcmc posteriors after importance reweighting; full cross-spectra constrain each link's optical metrology noise amplitude to $1\%$. when marginalizing over glitches or massive black hole binary transients, estimation errors remain flat up to transient signal-to-noise ratios of several hundred, whereas ignoring them severely biases likelihood fits. under time-varying spline noise levels, realistic glitch rates, and gaps up to one day long, posterior coverage remains nominal or conservative across $\sim 10^4$ simulations. we test coverage in the local neighborhood of a given observation by introducing a novel importance-weighted localized simulation-based calibration test. we find flow matching slightly better calibrated than diffusion in simpler regimes and observe modest gains from physics-aware template inputs. finally, we outline how these networks can initialize the noise and stochastic blocks of a lisa global fit.
